# AeroLife: Turbofan Remaining Useful Life Estimation

UCS321 project using public NASA C-MAPSS FD001. 

**Simulated turbofan data generated by NASA's C-MAPSS model; not measured engine data.** No affiliation with Rolls-Royce and no operational validation.

The project owner authorized Decision A (simulation benchmark) on 2026-10-20. This does not claim faculty approval. The original dataset investigation is retained in FEASIBILITY.md.

## Dataset

Public NASA catalog: https://data.nasa.gov/dataset/cmapss-jet-engine-simulated-data

Direct archive: https://data.nasa.gov/docs/legacy/CMAPSSData.zip

The archive was downloaded directly from NASA into data/raw/CMAPSSData.zip and extracted into data/raw/CMAPSSData/. SHA-256 hashes are recorded in data/provenance_manifest.json. Only FD001 is used: 100 training engines and 100 official test engines. Of the training engines, 80 are used for fitting and 20 for validation. See docs/dataset_card.md for parsing, labels and provenance.

## Run on Windows

The existing .venv has the dependencies installed:

```powershell
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m streamlit run app/streamlit_app.py
```

Open http://localhost:8501. The dashboard loads the saved LSTM from artifacts/v0.2.0/ and shows recorded test-engine replay and evaluation reports.

## Reproduce

For a fresh checkout, create a Python virtual environment and install requirements.txt. Download and extract the NASA archive to the paths above before running ingestion. The requirements file records the original tested package versions; the current installed environment was used for this training run.

```powershell
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts/ingest.py
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts/make_splits.py
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts/train.py
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts/evaluate.py
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest -q
```

Training fits four baselines and three LSTM seeds. It selects the LSTM seed by validation loss only and saves model.keras, preprocessor.json, metadata.json, predictions and histories. Configurations are in configs/config.yaml and configs/dataset_spec.yaml. No sequence-length ablation has been run.

## Results

Official FD001 test evaluation uses the final 30-cycle window of each of the 100 test engines and uncapped official RUL labels. The selected LSTM (seed 42) achieved MAE 13.47 cycles and RMSE 19.14 cycles. Random Forest performed better: MAE 10.83 and RMSE 14.55 cycles. All 65 automated tests passed.

See PROJECT_STATUS.md, docs/model_card.md and reports/tables/test_comparison.csv. Figures are in reports/figures/.

## Data and evaluation safeguards

- Original publisher files remain unchanged; ingestion verifies their hashes.
- Engine groups are split before windowing; official test engines never enter fitting or validation.
- Preprocessing is fitted on training engines only; imputation and rolling features are causal.
- Engine IDs, RUL labels, failure times and hidden health parameters are excluded from model inputs.
- Windows never cross engines; fewer than 30 observations produces an insufficient-history response.
- Dashboard replay truncates history before inference. Ground truth is retrospective only.
- Test histories stop before failure; their future failure times are reconstructed solely from official labels for retrospective scoring.
- Maintenance thresholds are teaching examples and do not support aircraft maintenance or dispatch decisions.

## Layout

- src/aerolife/: dataset adapter, preprocessing, windows, baselines, RNNs, inference and reporting
- scripts/: ingestion, splits, training, evaluation, ablation and prediction entry points
- app/: six-page Streamlit dashboard
- tests/: pipeline, label alignment, causality, saved inference and dashboard checks
- configs/: experiment settings and dataset specification
- docs/: dataset/model cards, limitations and historical assignment materials
- artifacts/v0.2.0/: trained LSTM and saved outputs
- reports/: evaluation tables and figures
